title: Store sessions on Linux and Windows, in memory on cloud machines, with per-key locks
description: Owner: Papyrus session. stores/secret_service.py, stores/kernel_keyring.py (probe first: Docker's default seccomp blocks keyctl/add_key), stores/agent.py (memory-only, 0600 Unix socket, '<product> auth agent --status|stop', never on disk), stores/windows.py (Credential Manager; refresh token only, 2,560-byte blob limit), in that order after macOS, each failing closed with recovery guidance and never plaintext. Backends named explicitly. locks.py: one fcntl/LockFileEx lock per key. Specs with fake backends; locked/absent stores; concurrent refresh and logout; symlink and permission refusal; fresh child processes; CI on Linux, macOS and Windows.

comments.author: home
comments.text: Implementation is on branch feature/stores-and-locks, PR https://github.com/AnthusAI/cli-login/pull/4 (CI green on all six jobs; not merged). Covers Windows locks, Secret Service, kernel keyring, memory agent (Linux/macOS only), Windows Credential Manager and ordered store selection.

comments.author: home
comments.text: Done in #4 (merged, green on ubuntu/macos/windows x 3.10/3.13): Secret Service, kernel keyring, memory agent, Windows Credential Manager with crash-safe chunks, cross-platform per-key locks, fail-closed selection. Real backends exercised in CI: Windows locks + Credential Manager, gnome-keyring under dbus-run-session, kernel keyring, agent over a real socket. Fakes only: macOS Keychain. Gap: no memory agent on Windows (Credential Manager only). Follow-up commit keeps specs and the plaintext test FileStore out of the wheel and broker zip.
